title: POC scoping - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private - FinSolve
summary: Initial POC scoping for FinSolve to evaluate deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, cost), workload sizing, benchmark plan, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and timeline. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share security pack and pricing, run a baseline benchmark on hosted, and schedule dedicated sizing session.
topics: Benchmark plan: test dataset, telemetry, SLA targets
Deployment decision factors: data residency, regulatory, cost vs latency
Timeline and next steps: 4-week POC proposal
action_items: Alex - Send security pack (SOC2 docs, encryption/KMS notes) by 2026-01-19
Priya - Prepare baseline benchmark script + sample prompts and upload to shared drive by 2026-01-20
Liam - Provide representative traffic profile (qps, token distribution) by 2026-01-18
Nadia - Share regulatory/data residency constraints and approved regions by 2026-01-18
Daniel - Schedule follow-up technical deep dive for Dedicated sizing week of 2026-01-25
next_steps: Redwood to run hosted baseline benchmark using customer's sample prompts
Customer to review security pack and confirm if Private deployment is required
Schedule Dedicated sizing session if hosted doesn't meet latency/throughput targets
Agree on POC timeline and success criteria (SLA targets, cost envelope)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Marta Ruiz (FinSolve Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Jing Wei (Infra), Carlos Mendes (Product), Nadia Khan (Security)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off, I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account. Priya will do the technical bits. quick agenda: confirm success criteria, go over workload sizing, propose a benchmark plan and discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs.
[00:18] Marta: Hi all, thanks, looking forward. Our main ask is: can we get sub-200ms token latency at our peak and keep per-token cost reasonable. Also strict data controls — some PII flows in logs.
[00:32] Priya: got it. quick clarifying q: is that 200ms end-to-end or inference-only?
[00:36] Liam: inference-only, as close to the model response latency as possible — doorway to the user. Our front-end adds about 80ms.
[00:45] Priya: okay that helps. can you share QPS and token distribution? even ballpark helps sizing.
[00:51] Jing: currently peak is about 300 req/sec for the feature, avg session 150 tokens, though we've seen spikes to 500 qps in experiments.
[01:05] Alex: perfect, that's the workload we'll scope. quick note on definitions: Hosted = Redwood API (multi-tenant), Dedicated = reserved GPU pools for you, Private = VPC or on-prem with customer-managed network and KMS.
[01:20] Carlos: what's the difference in SLAs and observability? we need per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdowns.
[01:28] Daniel: Redwood Console gives per-route/model dashboards, token/latency breakdowns, and tracing hooks — same surface across modes but retention/ingress differs by plan.
[01:40] Nadia: on compliance, we need to know about encryption at rest, KMS integration, and audit logs. Any SOC2/ISO artifacts?
[01:48] Alex: yes we'll send the security pack after this call. we have SOC2 and ISO summaries; for Private we support customer KMS/HSM and audit log export.
[01:58] Priya: returning to perf: for 300 qps and 150 tokens/session, continuous batching and KV cache behavior matter a lot. If you have conversational workloads with repetition, prefix KV cache will reduce per-token compute. we need sample prompts.
[02:15] Marta: we'll share 500 sample chats and the distribution.
[02:20] Priya: great. benchmark plan i propose: week 1 — hosted baseline with your samples, measure latency P50/P95/P99, cost; week 2 — if hosted miss targets, spin up Dedicated sizing (GPU types, batch sizes), run dedicated benchmarks; week 3 — optional Private proof (if needed) — same tests in VPC.
[02:39] Liam: sounds reasonable. how long does it take to get Dedicated reserved up?
[02:43] Alex: provisioning for a POC can be done in a few days for dev sizing; production-grade reserved pools typically a couple weeks depending on capacity and region.
[02:52] Jing: what instances / GPUs do you generally use for Dedicated?
[02:55] Priya: we commonly use A100-80GB and H100 for larger models, and cheaper quantized paths for 8-bit setups on T4-like hardware; kernel selection happens automatically in the runtime.
[03:07] Carlos: any rough cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
[03:11] Alex: hosted is pay-as-you-go, easier to start; Dedicated gives better unit economics at scale due to reserved capacity. for an estimate we need your qps profile and retention. I'll share a model-based cost estimate.
[03:23] Nadia: private deployment — what's the network pattern? does traffic egress through Redwood?
[03:28] Priya: Private keeps inference in your VPC and control plane can be customer-managed; optional on-prem package if air-gap required. logs and telemetry can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[03:40] Marta: decision factors for us are: if hosted meets latency and security, we prefer it for speed; otherwise Dedicated unless regulators force Private. correct?
[03:49] Alex: yep that's the typical path. Hosted first for fast iteration, Dedicated for predictable throughput and better unit cost, Private only when policy requires.
[03:58] Liam: what about failover? if Dedicated nodes get overloaded can requests fall back to Hosted?
[04:02] Priya: yes we support smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants in another tier or hosted pool, per policy.
[04:12] Carlos: how do you measure quality regressions? we need eval hooks.
[04:16] Daniel: Redwood Optimize has evals tied to prompt sets and regression alerts, we can wire your test set into the pipeline.
[04:25] Marta: okay, success criteria proposal: P50 < 120ms inference, P95 < 220ms inference, throughput sustaining 300 qps for 5-minute windows, no significant quality drop vs current baseline; cost per 1k tokens under our target (we'll provide target).
[04:43] Priya: that's actionable. for the hosted baseline we'll capture P50/P95/P99 and cost and then iterate.
[04:50] Jing: any gotchas on KV cache or batching we should be aware of?
[04:54] Priya: yes, sequence length distribution affects batching efficiency — long contexts reduce batch sizes and increase latency. also ensure you warm the KV cache for chat flows. transcription note: folks sometimes say K V cache in the transcript.
[05:07] Marta: timeline wise we want a decision in 4 weeks. is that realistic?
[05:11] Alex: yes. Proposed timeline: 1 week to run hosted baseline and review, 1 week for dedicated sizing if needed, 1-2 weeks buffer for security review / Private evaluation. total ~3-4 weeks.
[05:22] Liam: who owns the benchmark infra for hosted tests?
[05:26] Priya: Redwood can run the hosted load tests with your dataset and provide traces. alternatively, you can run the client-side load from your infra and we provide test script. we'll do both if helpful.
[05:36] Carlos: ok, what about data retention and logs — can we disable storing transcripts?
[05:40] Alex: yes. Hosted has controls for retention and PII redaction; Private gives you full control. we'll document specifics in the security pack.
[05:50] Nadia: for compliance we need SSO/SAML mapping and RBAC for model access. support?
[05:54] Daniel: yes we support SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles, and audit logging across modes.
[06:02] Marta: any rough numbers on cost for Dedicated for our profile?
[06:05] Alex: preliminary back-of-envelope: sustaining 300 qps with 150 tokens -> depends on model size. small LLMs quantized can be X, if you need 13B/70B class models cost ramps — we'll send a detailed estimate.
[06:16] Priya: also note quantization profile recommendations — sometimes a 4-bit/8-bit profile keeps quality but cuts cost. Redwood Optimize will suggest profiles per workload.
[06:27] Liam: ok that's helpful. next steps recap?
[06:30] Alex: I'll share security pack and pricing model; Priya will share benchmark script and run hosted baseline; Liam/Jing will send traffic profile and sample prompts; Daniel will schedule Dedicated sizing session week of 2026-01-25.
[06:46] Marta: sounds good. any other questions?
[06:50] Nadia: just to confirm, if we want Private we need a separate procurement route?
[06:54] Alex: yes Private is typically enterprise licensing + support; we'll loop legal/sales.
[07:00] Carlos: thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
